text:
Nick Foligno is 39 and still has nights that belong to him. On Nov. 21 in Vancouver he scored the go-ahead goal with 1:58 left in the third, his second of the season and his first since opening night, per NHL.com's Heather Rule. NHL.com's headline told the best part: "Foligno brothers connect for late lead." Marcus, his younger brother, is a teammate in Minnesota. The Canucks tied it and won in overtime, but the moment stood.

The rest of his season is a depth role played honestly. He was out of the lineup from Oct. 6 to Nov. 7, and since then he has played about 10 minutes a night. He has 4 points in 11 games on only 6 shots, and two goals on 0.75 expected goals (the quality of his chances) is finishing nobody should count on. His top speed and shot speed both rank in the bottom tenth of the league, which surprises no one. His value lives elsewhere: Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.1 wins above replacement last season, most of it from even-strength defense. The King Clancy winner of 2016-17 is still doing the job he's done for years.
headline: Nick Foligno, 39, still finds his moments
